chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام regarding Maghrib: Sometimes we perform salat while we fear that the sun may still be behind the mountain, or that the mountain may have merely screened it from us. He said: “You are not required to climb the mountain.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose setting determines the prayer time
key_terms.الْجَبَلِ: the mountain that may obstruct direct sight of the sun
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the time of Maghrib salat at sunset
key_terms.سَتَرَنَا: screened or concealed from our view

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to climb a mountain to confirm sunset before praying Maghrib?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time of Maghrib salat when natural obstructions like a mountain may affect visibility of the sun. Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام states that one is not obligated to undertake hardship, such as climbing a mountain, in order to verify sunset.
